Plot niche breadth curves

Source: R/iai_curve.R
plot.iai_curve.Rd

Plots the curves from iai_curve(): one line per species with bootstrap bands (dotted), a point at each species' density-independent value (at its own spillover abundance), the asymptote (density-dependent value) as a short horizontal dash at the right, and preference reversals (crosses). Beyond the largest total observed at any site of a species, the curve is drawn as a thinner line: there it extrapolates the fitted isodars.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'iai_curve'
plot(
  x,
  species = NULL,
  x_axis = c("log_abundance", "relative"),
  abundances = NULL,
  crossings = FALSE,
  legend = TRUE,
  col = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

Output of iai_curve().

species

Optional species to plot (default: all).

x_axis

"log_abundance" (total abundance, log scale) or "relative" (total abundance / spillover abundance, log scale; every species' DI value is then at 1).

abundances

Optional total abundances to mark with vertical lines ("log_abundance" only).

crossings

If TRUE, marks the totals where two species' curves cross (open circles; "log_abundance" only).

legend

TRUE (default) adds a legend (up to 12 species) in a corner free of curves and bands, or above the plot if there is none; a position such as "topleft" or "bottomright" (see graphics::legend()), or "outside" (above the plot), places it there; FALSE omits it.

col

Colours, one per species (default: the current palette).

...

Passed to graphics::plot().

Value

x, invisibly.

See also

iai_curve()
